sentences: The young Spanish princess Margarita stands among her maids of honor, a court dwarf, and a dog.
But on the left, Velázquez himself stands before a huge canvas and looks straight out at us.
In the mirror on the back wall, the king and queen appear, faint and blurred.
So whoever the painter is portraying, and wherever we are standing, it is the place of the king and queen.
By scrambling the roles of viewer, viewed, and painter, this picture has kept philosophers and artists arguing for centuries.
The red cross on the painter's chest was added after he was knighted, a few years after the painting was finished.
